simple.meaning: שֹׁעַל (shôʻal) is a Hebrew object word meaning “the palm ; by extension, a handful.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 1 Kings 20:10. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שֹׁעַל (H8168) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: שֹׁעַל (shôʻal) / H8168 is traced through 1 Kings 20:10, Isaiah 40:12, Ezekiel 13:19 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.short: the palm ; by extension, a handful
definitions.full: H8168. shoal [ שֹׁ֫עַל ] noun [masculine] hollow hand, handful ; — 1 hollow hand: suffix בְּשָׁעֳלוֺ Isa 40:12 (figurative of ׳י holding waters). 2 handful: plural שְׁעָלִים 1Kin 20:10 (dust, in hyperb.); construct שְׂעֹרִים שַׁעֲלֵי (as if from [ שַׁ֫עַל ] Kö ii. l. 35 ) Ezek 13:19 handfuls of barley.
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to hollow out;

occurrences.englishText: Ben Hadad sent to him, and said, “The gods do so to me, and more also, if the dust of Samaria will be enough for handfuls for all the people who follow me.”
Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand,

You have profaned me among my people for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread, to kill the souls who should not die, and to save the souls alive who should not live, by your lying to my people who listen to lies.’
